using Statistics
using Base64
using CairoMakie
using Makie

function main()
    # Read all input from stdin
    input_data = read(STDIN, String)
    
    # Check if input is empty
    if isempty(input_data)
        println("Error: Empty input")
        Base.exit(1)
        return
    end

    # Parse CSV
    # Split by newlines, then by commas
    lines = split(input_data, '\n')
    
    # Filter out empty lines
    lines = filter(!isempty, lines)
    
    if isempty(lines)
        println("Error: No data found in input")
        Base.exit(1)
        return
    end

    # First line is header
    header = split(lines[1], ',')
    
    # Check if header is empty
    if isempty(header)
        println("Error: Empty header")
        Base.exit(1)
        return
    end

    # Last column index
    num_cols = length(header)
    last_col_idx = num_cols

    # Prepare data structure: Vector of Vectors
    data = Vector{Vector{Union{Nothing, Any}}}()

    # Parse data rows
    for i in 2:length(lines)
        line = lines[i]
        # Handle trailing newline issues if any
        if !isempty(line)
            values = split(line, ',')
            
            # Ensure we have enough columns
            if length(values) >= last_col_idx
                # Extract last column values
                col_values = [v for v in values]
                
                # Store data
                push!(data, col_values)
            else
                # Row has fewer columns than header, skip
            end
        end
    end

    # Check if we have any data rows
    if isempty(data)
        println("Error: No data rows found")
        Base.exit(1)
        return
    end

    # Extract last column values, ignoring missing/invalid
    values = []
    for row in data
        if length(row) >= last_col_idx
            val = row[last_col_idx]
            # Check if value is valid (not nothing, not NaN, not Inf)
            if val !== nothing
                # Try to convert to Float64
                try
                    f = parse(Float64, string(val))
                    if isnan(f) || isinf(f)
                        # Skip NaN and Inf
                        continue
                    else
                        push!(values, f)
                    end
                catch
                    # Skip invalid numbers
                    continue
                end
            end
        end
    end

    # Check if we have any valid values
    if isempty(values)
        println("Error: No valid numerical values found in the last column")
        Base.exit(1)
        return
    end

    # Compute skewness
    # Using the Pearson's second moment coefficient formula (standard in Julia Statistics package)
    skewness = skewness(values)

    # Print result
    # Format as floating point number
    println(skewness)
end

main()
